content.comment_body: I need to measure temperature in 0.1 degree increments, but when using PT1000 settings on [product_name], I only get 0.25 degree steps, likely because the system is limited to 1000 steps for its inputs. If I adjust the measurement range to -500 to 500, with a gain of 1.00 and offset of -500, will this solve my problem? My measurement needs are between -20 and +50 degrees. Is this adjustment sufficient, or do I need to use a different sensor?

This isn't feasible with the current setup. The [product_name] analog module supports a temperature range of -50 to 200°C. For 0.1°C resolution, you'd need an external PT1000 transmitter configured for a 100°C span, such as -50 to 50°C or -30 to 70°C. The transmitter should provide either a 0-10V or 0/4-20mA output to achieve the desired resolution.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are running into limitations with PT1000 temperature measurement accuracy on [product_name], only obtaining 0.25°C increments because the system hardware permits 1000 input steps. Modifying input settings does not resolve the limitation, and users seeking finer resolution will need alternative solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to deliver temperature measurement increments as fine as 0.1°C when configured with a PT1000 sensor.
